title: Week 5 MFPI analysis: Tupelo High School leads the statewide rankings
dek: What moved in the Week 5 Mississippi Football Power Index, computed from verified results through Sep 29.
author: MFPI automated analysis

sources.label: MHSAA official score center (schedules and scores)
Statewide media rankings used for the Media Rank inputs

limitations: Generated from the published snapshot; no games after the cutoff are included.
Media Rank and Media Strength of Schedule contribute 20% of every rating; MFPI's own score-based model contributes 80%.
No player, injury, coaching or game-narrative information is used or implied.

sections.heading: The top of the statewide rankings
paragraphs: [[tupelo]] (5-0) is No. 1 for the 5th straight published week. MFPI rating: decreased 0.3 points to 95.9. In the latest window it beat [[west-point]] (currently No. 88) 34-6 on the road on Sep 25.
No. 2 [[diberville]] (5-0, 7A): ranking unchanged at No. 2; rating increased 0.3 points to 94.6. It beat [[harrison-central]] (currently No. 80) 42-7 at home on Sep 25.
No. 3 [[warren-central]] (5-0, 6A): ranking unchanged at No. 3; rating increased 0.4 points to 92.6. It beat [[madison-central]] (currently No. 31) 42-21 at home on Sep 25.
No. 4 [[starkville]] (4-1, 7A): ranking unchanged at No. 4; rating decreased 0.7 points to 91.2. It lost to [[brandon]] (currently No. 8) 31-38 at home on Sep 25.
No. 5 [[gulfport]] (3-1, 7A): ranking unchanged at No. 5; rating unchanged at 90.9. It beat [[pascagoula]] (currently No. 66) 41-7 at home on Sep 25.

sections.heading: Classification leaders
paragraphs: Class ranks are the statewide order filtered to one classification; MFPI never recalculates a separate class rating.
Class 2A: [[heidelberg]] replaced [[east-webster]] at No. 1.

sections.heading: Results that raised ratings most
paragraphs: The largest rating increases among teams with a verified result in this window. A rating can also move without a game, because every opponent's rating is re-solved each week.
[[wilkinson-county]] (+17.2 to 57.2, now No. 92) beat [[sacred-heart]] (currently No. 169) 44-3 at home on Sep 25.
[[nanih-waiya]] (+14.4 to 51.1, now No. 107) beat [[water-valley]] (currently No. 100) 48-36 on the road on Sep 25.
[[heidelberg]] (+14.1 to 76.4, now No. 36) beat [[leake-central]] (currently No. 44) 47-0 on the road on Sep 25.
[[mooreville]] (+10.2 to 43.3, now No. 136) beat [[mantachie]] (currently No. 184) 42-0 at home on Sep 25.
[[new-hope]] (+10.0 to 74.4, now No. 41) beat [[houston]] (currently No. 95) 34-7 on the road on Sep 25.
The full list of movers is in the [[risers-and-fallers:2026-week-05-risers-and-fallers]] analysis.

sections.heading: Schedule strength
paragraphs: MFPI strength of schedule is the average current rating of every completed opponent, expressed as a statewide percentile (100 is the strongest schedule in this week's field, not a perfect grade). The five strongest schedules: [[west-point]] (0-4, SOS percentile 100.0); [[oxford]] (4-1, SOS percentile 99.6); [[brandon]] (4-1, SOS percentile 99.1); [[west-harrison]] (2-3, SOS percentile 98.7); [[madison-central]] (2-3, SOS percentile 98.2).

Teams that have played furthest above their own classification (average class steps up, games up in class): [[okolona]] (1A, +2.50, 4 up); [[poplarville]] (4A, +2.00, 5 up); [[lumberton]] (1A, +2.00, 4 up); [[byers]] (1A, +2.00, 4 up); [[scott-central]] (2A, +1.80, 5 up).

sections.heading: Data notes and limitations
paragraphs: Snapshot generated September 29, 2026 at 1:41 PM Central with a cutoff of September 29 at 11:00 AM Central, formula MFPI-3.2.
567 of 578 game listings due by the cutoff had verified scores (98.1%); the rest count as unavailable, never as losses or 0-0 results.

No verified results were linked to [[northside]] for this cutoff. Their ratings are provisional and rest on class, media and neutral inputs; their positions should not be read as the product of games.
Opponent ranks in this article are the opponent's rank in this snapshot, not its rank on the day the game was played, unless a sentence says otherwise.
